solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Balls involved with dodgy turn, taking Strictly round the country?

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable and crooked, so the letters are bent out of their given order

blocks.note: two balls are two round O shapes

explanation.surface: A dancer's balls and turns go wrong as the Strictly show travels the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly Come Dancing is a BBC ballroom show whose stars go on a nationwide live tour each year.
explanation.definitionFit: A touring show travels from venue to venue, which is what the Strictly live production does across Britain.

clue.text: Perverse alternative, sticking end of dick in leafstalk to get very erect

indicators.note: perverse means contrary or turned the wrong way, so the word is read backwards
the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept
sticking something in a stem pushes it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: chard is a vegetable grown for its leaf stalks

explanation.surface: A smutty picture of a perverse choice and a firm erection, in Private Eye's usual style.
explanation.walkthrough: The K goes in after the first letter of the vegetable, splitting it as C and HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock hard is an intensified phrase for stiff or firm, so it describes something extremely erect.

clue.text: (& 25dn.) "Balls' comeback urgent" – dope reveals what we don't want to hear

definitions.text: what we don't want to hear

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the politician's name comes back to front

blocks.note: Ed Balls is a former Labour shadow chancellor
a pressing matter is an urgent one
dope is slang for information or the latest news

explanation.surface: A tabloid line about Ed Balls's urgent return, with an insider's dope revealing unwelcome tidings.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Balls is a British Labour politician; his first name reversed starts the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad tidings are exactly the sort of report people would rather not be told, gloomy and disheartening.

clue.text: (& 13dn.) Sun exposure led to this cutting short of PM with the anxious trembling?

indicators.note: cutting short a name removes its tail, so the last letter goes
trembling shakes things about, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: Edward Heath was Conservative Prime Minister 1970-74

explanation.surface: Too long in the sun has left someone shaky and anxious, like a former PM.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted Heath was a British Prime Minister; dropping his last letter leaves the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Overheating from too much sunshine causes collapse, dizziness and trembling, the medical condition named here.

clue.text: Cabinet damaged by this 'Conservative Way' U-turn?

indicators.note: a U-turn heads back the way it came, so the combined letters are read backwards

blocks.note: Tory is the everyday name for a Conservative
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A government Cabinet ruined by another Conservative policy U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cabinet is not the government but a piece of wooden furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a fungus that decays timber, so a wooden cupboard can be destroyed by it.

clue.text: (& 16ac.) Big Brother sort of thing – crap sort here's no different

indicators.note: made different, the letters are arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Grumbling that the latest surveillance law is the same old rubbish as ever.
explanation.walkthrough: Snoopers' Charter is the nickname for Britain's Investigatory Powers Act, which lets the state monitor internet use.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Brother is Orwell's all-watching state, and this legislation is mocked as granting mass surveillance powers.

clue.text: Skimpy boxers do, so extend tops

indicators.note: the tops of words are their first letters, so only those are taken

explanation.surface: Boxers in skimpy shorts are told to stretch their tops.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something thin, scanty or meagre in amount.

clue.text: English otherwise upset, flooded by American cash

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so in a down-style reading the word is flipped backwards
something flooded is surrounded on all sides, so these letters sit inside another word

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
US is the standard abbreviation for American
or offers an otherwise, an alternative

explanation.surface: The English are upset that American money is pouring into the country.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the currency of the eurozone, so plural euros are money, ready funds.

clue.text: Economics, say, since getting wrecked by committed Exit leaders

definitions.note: an example standing for the wider category

indicators.note: a wreck is smashed apart, so the letters are scattered and rebuilt
leaders are the front runners, so each word gives its first letter

explanation.surface: The British economy has been wrecked since committed Brexiteers took charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' signals that economics is an example: it is often called the dismal science.
explanation.definitionFit: Economics is classed as a social science, one branch of systematic knowledge and study.

clue.text: see 26ac.
Trump, dismissing politician on radio, snapped "This is USA's path now!"

indicators.note: dismissing someone sends them away, so those letters are dropped
snapped means broken, so the letters fall apart and recombine

blocks.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is removed

explanation.surface: Trump, having sacked an official, barks on air about America's direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a course leading to disaster, which the setter suggests America is now following.

clue.text: A Republican state's a Republican state

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A tautological political observation: a state that votes Republican is a Republican state.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue repeats itself: the first half is wordplay, the second half the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkansas is a southern US state that votes solidly for the Republican Party in elections.

clue.text: see 18dn.
Welcoming next disaster, the leading characters in election debacle "reach out"

indicators.note: welcoming takes a guest in, so the outer letters hold the rest inside
a disaster leaves things in chaos, so the word's letters are thrown into disorder
leading characters are the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: After an election debacle, a party braces for the next disaster and tries to reach out to voters.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch or stretch out a hand is to lengthen it toward something, so the verbs match.

clue.text: see 4dn.
Elected after abuse – "Lose ego and give something in return!"

indicators.note: losing the self takes away the first-person letter from a word
after places one piece behind the other in the order they are written

blocks.note: a tirade is a torrent of abuse
I is the ego, oneself; it is removed
a party elected is in power

explanation.surface: A newly elected figure, after a barrage of insults, is told to drop the ego and give back.
explanation.definitionFit: Trading in means handing over an old item as part payment for a new one, an exchange.

clue.text: "Crush Right!" – female leader failing to hold Germany's centre

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, the only one kept
failing to hold on means letting go, so a letter drops out

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
an empress is a woman ruling an empire

explanation.surface: A right-wing call to arms aimed at a woman leader who failed to keep German support.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress is to subdue or put down by force, the same as crushing a revolt.

clue.text: see 6ac.
Theresa's heart goes to vacillating buffoon: "Leave your mark on someone"

indicators.note: the heart of a name is its middle letter
vacillating means wavering back and forth, so the letters shift position

explanation.surface: Theresa May's sympathies go to a dithering clown who is told to make his mark.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa is Theresa May, the Prime Minister; the buffoon suggests Boris Johnson.
explanation.definitionFit: When a quality rubs off on a person it transfers to them, influencing them by contact.

clue.text: (& 12dn.) 'Community member' row buries Miliband

indicators.note: burying something puts it inside, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: a rant is a noisy row or tirade
Ed Miliband is a former Labour Party leader

explanation.surface: A party row in which Ed Miliband is drowned out by his own community.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Miliband led Britain's Labour Party; 'red' is also the party's colour, adding to the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ants live in organised colonies, so each insect is one member of a social group.

clue.text: Forlorn thing: one has to replace ring

indicators.note: replacing swaps one thing out for another in the same position

blocks.note: a ring is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A lonely figure finds a lost ring replaced by something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Abject describes wretched hopelessness, much like a desolate, miserable state.

clue.text: 20% of presidents, encumbered by uncontrolled guns, recoiled

indicators.note: a fifth of a ten-letter word is its opening two letters
encumbered means weighed down and surrounded, so these letters go inside
uncontrolled letters run wild into a different order

explanation.surface: A fifth of US presidents, weighed down by lax gun laws, shrank back.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sprung has leapt back suddenly, like a spring released, as a recoil does.

clue.text: Moderate Trump – i.e. tempered once temperature's dropped

indicators.note: dropped means let fall away, so that letter leaves the word
tempered means worked and reshaped, like metal, so the letters are remixed

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for temperature; it is removed

explanation.surface: A plea for Trump to calm down once the political temperature falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb: to referee or preside.
explanation.definitionFit: An umpire moderates a contest, adjudicating between sides as an impartial referee.

clue.text: Conservative getting jail sentence: "it flies!"

blocks.note: blue is the Conservative Party colour
bird is British slang for a prison term

explanation.surface: A Tory is jailed, and the time seems to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing bird' is British slang for serving prison time, from rhyming slang bird-lime, time.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluebird is a songbird, and like most birds it travels through the air on wings.

clue.text: Queen secures pathetic Nige's surrender

indicators.note: something pathetic is feeble and falls apart, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: The monarch obtains Nigel Farage's feeble capitulation.
explanation.walkthrough: Nige is Nigel Farage, the British Brexit campaigner and party leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to give up or relinquish a post or position, yielding it to others.

clue.text: Taking Boris's lead, needed tip – sad state of Britain now

definitions.note: a noun phrase defining an adjectival phrase

indicators.note: a name's lead is its first letter
sad here means sorry or wretched, so the letters are in a sorry jumble

explanation.surface: Following Boris Johnson has turned Britain into a sad rubbish dump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' is British for a rubbish dump, feeding the surface picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter says the nation now owes huge sums, the condition of heavy borrowing.

clue.text: see 3dn.
(& 10ac.) Abstain together with Labour, by which you soon achieve your goal

definitions.text: by which you soon achieve your goal

blocks.note: to fast is to abstain from food

explanation.surface: Joining Labour in abstaining from a vote is a quick route to getting what you want.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour looks like the political party, but here it is plain toil.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick progress or efficient effort reaches an aim promptly, which is what the phrase describes.

clue.text: Southern boat people bleed

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
a crew are the people working a boat

explanation.surface: Migrants arriving by boat from the south are being bled dry.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleed someone or screw them is to extort money, taking everything they have.

clue.text: Comprehensive's done for – it holds sod all

indicators.note: holding something keeps it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: someone through is finished, done for
sod all is British slang for nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A failing comprehensive school is finished and has nothing left in it.
explanation.walkthrough: A comprehensive is a British state secondary school, but here it is the adjective meaning complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean complete and detailed, covering every part fully without omission.
